# zumime

A file’s name says what someone hopes it is; its bytes say what it is.
An upload named `invoice.pdf` can be a PNG, a `.docx` is a ZIP archive
inside, and a `.csv.gz` holds a CSV you cannot see until you open the
gzip. Before a parser starts, you want to know which of these you have,
and whether the file is encrypted or cut short.

zumime answers from both signals in one call and says whether they
agree. It has no dependencies and no system library, so it gives the
same answer on every machine.

- **The browser’s algorithm.** The byte answer is the [WHATWG MIME
  Sniffing Standard](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/), with its
  supplied type, no-sniff flag and contexts, checked against Go’s
  `net/http` sniff cases.
- **Containers and R’s own files.** ZIP entry names tell a Word document
  from a JAR, ISO base media brands tell an M4A from an MP4, and RDS,
  RData, Parquet, SQLite, Stata and SPSS files are known by their
  headers, checked against the fixtures of the JavaScript
  [file-type](https://github.com/sindresorhus/file-type) package.
- **A hierarchy.** Every type has a parent, ending at
  `application/octet-stream`, so an unknown ZIP-based format is still a
  ZIP, and an allowlist of `"image"` accepts every image.
- **What to know before opening.** The type inside a compression
  wrapper, encryption, completeness, line endings and a script’s
  interpreter, read from the same bytes.
- **The same answer everywhere.** No `mime.types`, no Windows registry,
  no libmagic: the extension table is generated from IANA’s registry and
  Apache httpd’s `mime.types`.

## Installation

Install zumime from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("zumime")
```

Or the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zumime")
```

## Usage

``` r

library(zumime)
```

Take a folder of uploads: a real PDF, a PNG that claims to be a PDF, a
compressed CSV and an R data file.

``` r

uploads <- tempfile("uploads")
dir.create(uploads)
writeLines("%PDF-1.7", file.path(uploads, "report.pdf"))
writeBin(as.raw(c(0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a)),
  file.path(uploads, "invoice.pdf"))
con <- gzfile(file.path(uploads, "sales.csv.gz"), "w")
writeLines(c("region,total", "north,10"), con)
close(con)
saveRDS(mtcars, file.path(uploads, "cars.rds"))

paths <- list.files(uploads, full.names = TRUE)
```

[`mime_type()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_type.md)
types each file from its bytes and from its name. `agree` is `FALSE` for
the PNG named `.pdf`, and `inner` names what the gzip holds:

``` r

files <- mime_type(paths)
files[c("type", "confidence", "by_name", "agree", "inner")]
#> <zumime_result: 4 rows>
#>                type confidence           by_name agree    inner
#> 1 application/x-rds   definite application/x-rds  TRUE     <NA>
#> 2         image/png   definite   application/pdf FALSE     <NA>
#> 3   application/pdf   definite   application/pdf  TRUE     <NA>
#> 4  application/gzip   definite  application/gzip  TRUE text/csv
```

[`mime_check()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_check.md)
asks only the allowlist question, from the bytes alone, since that is
the question you ask because names lie. Of the two files named `.pdf`,
one is:

``` r

setNames(mime_check(paths, "application/pdf"), basename(paths))
#>     cars.rds  invoice.pdf   report.pdf sales.csv.gz 
#>        FALSE        FALSE         TRUE        FALSE
```

[`mime_sniff()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_sniff.md)
runs the standard on bytes in hand, as a browser would on a response. A
`text/plain` label is one some servers send for anything, so the
standard checks it and finds binary bytes; under `nosniff` the label
stands:

``` r

png <- readBin(file.path(uploads, "invoice.pdf"), "raw", 8)
mime_sniff(png, type = "text/plain")$type
#> [1] "application/octet-stream"
mime_sniff(png, type = "text/plain", no_sniff = TRUE)$type
#> [1] "text/plain"
```

Types form a hierarchy, so a question about a family covers its members:

``` r

docx <- "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document"
mime_parent(docx)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "application/zip"          "application/octet-stream"
mime_is(docx, "application/zip")
#> [1] TRUE
```

Every function starts with `mime_`, and every type is a canonical name
from the registry that
[`mime_types()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_types.md)
returns.

## Learn more

- [Checking an upload before you open
  it](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/articles/checking-an-upload.html)
  walks through an allowlist, the `agree`, `encrypted` and `complete`
  columns, and the incremental sniffer on a stream’s first chunk.
- The [reference](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/)
  documents every function, grouped by task.

## Related work

The byte answer follows the WHATWG MIME Sniffing Standard and is tested
against Go’s `net/http` sniff cases and the web-platform-tests
`mimesniff` fixtures. Container inspection follows
[file-type](https://github.com/sindresorhus/file-type),
[filetype](https://github.com/h2non/filetype) and
[mimetype](https://github.com/gabriel-vasile/mimetype); the extension
table is generated from the [IANA media types
registry](https://www.iana.org/assignments/media-types/) and Apache
httpd’s `mime.types`. No code is copied from any of them.

# Package index

## From bytes

The WHATWG sniffing algorithm, with zumime’s containers and formats.

- [`mime_sniff()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_sniff.md)
  : Sniff a type from bytes

## From the name

- [`mime_guess()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_guess.md)
  : Guess a type from a file name
- [`mime_extensions()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_extensions.md)
  : Extensions of a type

## Both, with the how-to-open columns

- [`mime_type()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_type.md)
  : Type files from their bytes and their names
- [`mime_check()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_check.md)
  : Is a file one of these types?

## The hierarchy

- [`mime_parent()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_parent.md)
  : The lineage of a type
- [`mime_is()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_is.md)
  : Is a type one of these?
- [`mime_types()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_types.md)
  : The type registry

## The MIME type record

- [`mime_parse()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_parse.md)
  [`mime_format()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_parse.md)
  : Parse and serialise MIME types

## Detectors for the session

- [`mime_register()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_register.md)
  [`mime_unregister()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_register.md)
  : Register a type for the session

## Streams

- [`mime_sniffer()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_sniffer.md)
  [`mime_push()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_sniffer.md)
  [`mime_finish()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/mime_sniffer.md)
  : Sniff a stream chunk by chunk

## The package

- [`zumime_info()`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/zumime_info.md)
  : Build information
- [`zumime`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/zumime-package.md)
  [`zumime-package`](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zumime/reference/zumime-package.md)
  : zumime: Media Type Detection from Bytes and File Names
